# Chris Lam

> Product Design Engineer for AI-native products, 14 years. "I design the product. I ship the code." Currently Co-Founder and CPTO at y30, voice AI for older adults and their caregivers. Open to senior or lead IC design-engineering roles, full-time, on small, fast, AI-native teams.

Chris Lam (Christopher Lam) is a product design engineer with 14 years shipping healthcare, creative, developer, and consumer software. He built his career in product design, including early roles at Clover Health, GoodRx, Pathstream, and StartPlaying, then deliberately deepened into production engineering. Today he owns products end to end: research, interaction design, design systems, React/TypeScript/Python implementation, agent architecture, evals, and production verification. He is seeking senior or lead IC design-engineering roles on AI-native teams.

Role family for matching: Product Design Engineer, Design Engineer, Lead Design Engineer, Staff Design Engineer, UX Engineer, Design Systems Engineer, AI Product Engineer. These describe the shape of role he is targeting and the work he does, not official titles he has held.

Location: remote in the US, based in Honolulu. He works West Coast hours and travels to the Bay Area or Seattle quarterly. He is not seeking relocation.

He is AI-native in how he works: he steers product, architecture, and systems, directs AI agents through implementation, and owns the judgment, code review, and safety gates.

He is currently Co-Founder and CPTO at y30, voice AI for older adults and their caregivers. y30 generates longitudinal conversational signals for clinician or caregiver review. It does not diagnose, screen for, or detect cognitive decline or any other condition, and it is not a medical device.

His exits, framed honestly and never as a trophy count: he was early at Clover Health and GoodRx (both later IPO'd), a rescue hire at Sharecare during its acquisition (which then went public), and did the 2014 TaskRabbit rebrand before IKEA acquired it. The signal is repeated high ownership at early or critical stages, not an exit count.

## Case studies
Full write-ups with artifacts, outcomes, and what went wrong. Index: https://whoischrislam.github.io/work/
- Pathstream (2019-2020, Senior Product Design Manager, first design hire): rebuilt the core lesson experience of a live learning platform mid-cohort without forcing a rewrite of 60-80 hours of existing course content; also the Labs PRD across students, instructors, and course authors. Success metrics were written but never measured, and the page says so. https://whoischrislam.github.io/work/pathstream.html
- Iodine (2017-2018, Lead Product Designer, first full-time designer): coupon find-and-redeem flow, conversion 2% to 5%; Webby for Best Health Website 2018. https://whoischrislam.github.io/work/iodine.html
- GoodRx Research (2017-2018): drug-page conversion, 10% lift mobile and 25% desktop; data visualizations referenced in the New York Times and on Good Morning America. https://whoischrislam.github.io/work/goodrx.html
- Clover Health Care Visit (2015-2016, Designer, second designer): nurse-practitioner home-visit app, about 7-8x ROI on visit-related revenue, 1-2 hours saved per nurse per night. https://whoischrislam.github.io/work/clover-care-visit.html
- Clover Health website (2015-2016): first website, shipped ahead of 2016 enrollment, extended to out-of-home. https://whoischrislam.github.io/work/clover-health-website.html
- TaskRabbit Tasker experience (2014-2015): owned the Tasker side through the 2014 rebrand; Tasker NPS recovered from about -5 to the mid-50s. https://whoischrislam.github.io/work/taskrabbit-tasker.html
- TaskRabbit Client experience (2014-2015): the move from bidding to direct hire. https://whoischrislam.github.io/work/taskrabbit-client.html

## Selected outcomes
- Clover Health (Designer, the second designer, joined pre-seed; later IPO'd): ~7-8x lift in nurse visit-related revenue, ~2 hours saved per nurse per day.
- Iodine, acquired by GoodRx (first full-time designer): coupon conversion 2% to 5%. Iodine.com won the Webby for Best Health Website in 2018; he was the product's designer. On GoodRx Research he built data visualizations referenced in the New York Times and on Good Morning America and ABC News, and 50-state prescription-price fact sheets with co-CEO Doug Hirsch, used in advocacy around S.2554 and S.2553 on drug price transparency.
- TaskRabbit (later acquired by IKEA): owned the Tasker experience; NPS recovered from about -5 to the mid-50s.
- Amazon: prototyped the buy-and-gift Prime flow projected to drive 1M+ new subscribers.
- Modus Create: shipped dark mode for JIRA and Confluence Cloud, 500K+ enterprise users.
- y30: built the voice pipeline (multi-provider, deep fallback) and a model-independent safety floor; 1,389 commits, 127 test files.
- PlaySesh (Co-Founder and CEO; company founded 2024, product shipped July 2025, ran to 2026): built 0 to 1 solo; 6,220 authorized Discord accounts, 138 Discord server installs, and 1,043 monthly active users at peak in January 2026, all organic.
  - Measurement note: these are three different measurements and are never interchangeable. Authorized accounts are Discord OAuth authorizations, not users and not installs. Server installs count servers the app was added to. MAU is unique users in the peak calendar month, January 2026, from PlaySesh's own analytics. Discord counts as of August 1, 2026.

## Selected engineering (systems depth, not commit counts)
- HogWare (solo, 2026): a WarioWare-style microgame gauntlet built from PostHog's five handbook values in about a week. PostHog is the backend: a HogQL leaderboard with in-query cheat protection behind a Cloudflare Worker, a live flag experiment, and a survey; a 32-check headless suite plays the game end to end.
- PlaySesh: authored the core real-time engine, a custom operation-based sync protocol on Cloudflare Durable Objects (authoritative ordering, hand-written WebSocket reconnection), after moving the product off an off-the-shelf canvas library. Primary engineer on the codebase.
- Evolve, Die, Repeat (solo Lua/Love2D game): a solver that proves every procedurally generated level is completable via a reachability search over the player's jump physics; from-scratch headless test harness, about 1,568 tests.
- y30: conversation flow as a deterministic state machine with the language model scoped to phrasing and warmth, plus a model-independent rule-based safety floor; about half of routing resolves with no model call.
- Engineering judgment: built y30's first version in TypeScript, then deliberately rewrote it in Python to fit the real-time voice framework, carrying the architecture and safety model across as a spec.
- Hand-built without AI: this site and its voice agent are vanilla JavaScript, no framework, down to audio codec detection and mobile keyboard handling.
- y30: an automated eval flywheel grades every conversation against a rubric and auto-files regressions as issues (metadata only, no transcript or PHI), so quality drops are caught without a human in the loop.
- y30: real-time emotion-aware delivery, the agent reads emotional cues and adapts its voice in the moment (for example, softening when a conversation turns to grief).
- y30: a provider-resilient voice pipeline that degrades gracefully across multiple STT, LLM, and TTS providers plus a separate speech-to-speech fallback, so a live call never breaks when one dependency fails.
